forces.title: Electrification Reshaping Component Value Pool Towards High-Tech
forces.description: Rising EV adoption is structurally reshaping the auto component value pool in India, shifting it significantly towards high-value-added, technology-intensive components. This includes batteries, motors, power electronics, semiconductors, sensors, controllers, thermal management systems, and embedded software. This transition, driven by increased electronics content in EVs, creates substantial new opportunities for manufacturers capable of producing these advanced systems, moving the industry from metal-intensive to software-enabled products.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Raw Material Volatility and Import Dependence Pose Profitability Risks
forces.description: The auto ancillary industry faces significant profitability pressures from volatility in raw material prices, higher freight costs, and evolving geopolitical developments. A key risk stems from continued dependence on imported critical components such as battery cells, semiconductors, rare earth minerals, and other technology-intensive parts. This reliance exposes manufacturers to global supply chain disruptions and cost fluctuations, necessitating strategic efforts to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities for greater value chain control.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Strengthening Global Integration & Auto Component Export Opportunities
forces.description: India's auto component exports have more than doubled from FY21 to FY26, projected to grow by 8% in FY27 to Rs 2,300 billion. This strong performance is driven by strengthening global automotive supply chain integration, improving domestic manufacturing capabilities, and India's inherent cost competitiveness. This trend represents a significant upside driver, enabling the industry to capture a larger share of global sourcing opportunities, diversify revenue streams, and enhance its international market presence, supported by government localisation initiatives.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Auto Component Industry Shifts to Electronics and Software-Enabled Systems
forces.description: The Indian auto component industry is undergoing a structural transformation, driven by evolving vehicle technologies, increasing electrification, premiumisation, and stricter safety and emissions regulations. Future growth is increasingly led by higher content per vehicle, electronics integration, and software-enabled systems. This marks an evolution from a traditional manufacturing-led sector to a more technology- and engineering-oriented ecosystem, with the value pool shifting away from metal-intensive products towards advanced electronics and software components.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: AI Transforms EV Sales to Personalised Advisory Experience
forces.description: The growing complexity of electric vehicles, encompassing charging infrastructure, battery health, and software features, necessitates greater customer guidance. AI is transforming automotive retail from product-selling to a personalized advisory experience, enabling dealerships to understand diverse customer needs and recommend tailored products, financing, and charging solutions. This AI-driven approach builds confidence, which is identified as a crucial enabler for accelerating mass-market EV adoption and enhancing customer satisfaction within the automotive sector.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: AI Improves Dealership Profitability and Customer Retention Across Lifecycle
forces.description: Integration of AI into customer relationship management and dealer management systems creates unified customer profiles, enabling AI-driven lead qualification, predictive marketing, and intelligent customer engagement throughout the ownership lifecycle. This technology drives productivity gains for dealerships by identifying high-intent customers and improving response quality, directly influencing profitability in a competitive market. Furthermore, it protects and expands aftersales revenue streams by fostering better customer retention, crucial for overall business health.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: AI Enables Predictive Maintenance and Operational Efficiency for Vehicles
forces.description: Modern connected vehicles and EVs generate vast operational data. AI-driven systems can proactively identify emerging issues related to battery performance, charging behavior, and software health, transforming dealerships into vehicle-health management providers. This capability is particularly impactful for commercial mobility segments like two-wheelers, three-wheelers, buses, and fleet operations, where vehicle uptime is directly linked to earnings. AI improves asset productivity, reliability, and profitability through predictive maintenance and route optimization.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: AI Boosts EV Adoption Through Customer Education and Brand Loyalty
forces.description: A significant barrier to EV adoption is consumer uncertainty regarding charging access, range performance, battery degradation, and resale value. AI-enabled customer journeys can address these concerns by providing personalized, ongoing support and information throughout the ownership lifecycle. This engagement strengthens customer confidence, improves satisfaction, and deepens brand loyalty, effectively reducing misinformation and anxiety. This proactive educational approach will be vital for fostering broader acceptance of electric vehicles.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Automotive Industry Shifting to Data-Centric Mobility with AI at Core
forces.description: The EV transition signifies a broader structural shift in the automotive industry from product-centric to data-centric mobility. In this new paradigm, customer intelligence, predictive engagement, and continuous relationships are becoming as critical as engineering excellence. AI applications, particularly those 'around the vehicle' such as sales, financing, service, charging, maintenance, and retention, are expected to define the future competitive landscape for automotive retail and the broader industry, reshaping operational models and value propositions.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Geopolitical Volatility and Crude Price Spikes Threaten Profit Margins
forces.description: The 'stop-start' dynamic of the US-Iran conflict has plunged the global economy into deep uncertainty, acutely impacting India due to its dependence on West Asian energy corridors. Sudden re-closures of the Strait of Hormuz immediately squeeze natural gas supply, threatening domestic inflation and compressing profit margins across manufacturing sectors, including automotive. The volatile crude oil prices and currency depreciation against the USD pose a serious challenge to macroeconomic stability and input costs for the industry.

forces.title: RBI's Credit Risk Framework to Unlock Capital for Lending
forces.description: The RBI's new Standardised Approach for credit risk (effective April 1, 2027) reduces risk weights for AA, BBB, and BB rating categories, estimated to release over Rs 58,000 crore in capital for banks across sectors including manufacturing. This capital relief is expected to support enhanced lending capacity, lower borrowing costs, and more favorable sanction terms for moderately rated borrowers. This creates a significant tailwind for the Automobiles & Components sector by improving access to financing for expansion and operations.

forces.title: Global Volatility Accelerates Tech Investments and De-risking Strategy
forces.description: Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty is not hindering but accelerating technological progress within the automotive industry. Companies are strategically doubling down on investments in digital and software foundations, strengthening data capabilities, and increasing strategic independence. This approach transforms external volatility into a catalyst for de-risking operations and supply chains through enhanced technology, rather than prompting a retreat from innovation. It reshapes investment priorities to build more resilient and adaptive business models.

forces.title: Automotive Sector Strengthens Data Sovereignty, Local Talent, Supply Chains
forces.description: Automotive companies are proactively enhancing data sovereignty audits across partner ecosystems, increasing onshore technology talent hiring, and improving data flows and infrastructure to support scenario planning and decision-making agility. This strategic focus on localization, data resilience, and de-risking technology and supply chains provides a significant tailwind. It enhances operational resilience, fosters greater control over critical assets, and improves responsiveness to external shocks, ultimately strengthening the sector's long-term competitiveness and stability.

forces.title: OEMs Prioritize AI Scaling and Data Contracts for Efficiency
forces.description: OEMs are actively progressing from initial AI use cases to systematic scaling across engineering, operations, and customer domains. Their strategic focus includes rationalizing platforms, enforcing domain data contracts ('golden paths'), embedding Security-by-Design into Software Defined Vehicles (SDV) stacks, and industrializing Machine Learning Operations (MLOps). These efforts indicate a strong commitment to integrating advanced technology to enhance vehicle development, manufacturing processes, and overall customer experience, acting as a significant tailwind for the automotive sector.

forces.title: Truck Manufacturers Scale Digital Twins and Simulation for Operations
forces.description: Truck manufacturers are rapidly advancing in operations-adjacent capabilities, particularly through the adoption of digital twins and simulation technologies. This focus is leading to coordinated rollouts of these technologies, which are expected to yield measurable impacts on efficiency and reliability. These investments signify a strong tailwind for the commercial vehicle segment (IN040102), driving improvements in vehicle design, testing, maintenance, and fleet management, ultimately enhancing the competitiveness and performance of commercial vehicles.

forces.title: Tier 1 Suppliers Diversify with Tech and M&A for Growth
forces.description: Tier 1 automotive suppliers are demonstrating strong leadership in scaling AI, data, cybersecurity, and simulation, achieving high capital efficiency. Strategically, they are repositioning 'Anything as a Service' (XaaS) as a diversification engine and transitioning their portfolio mix from volume-linked components to solution-led platforms. Targeted M&A and partnerships are being pursued to acquire software, data, and platform capabilities, accelerating their entry into industrial, mobility services, and energy ecosystems, thereby reducing dependence on OEM roadmaps and driving diversified growth.

forces.title: Ambitious EV Penetration Targets Fuel Advanced Component Demand
forces.description: The Indian government's ambitious objective for 30% EV market penetration by 2030 is significantly fueling demand for advanced components. This includes critical parts such as batteries, power electronics, and electric drivetrains, which are essential for electric vehicle manufacturing. This policy-driven demand creates a substantial tailwind for the auto-component industry (IN040104), driving innovation, investment, and capacity expansion in these high-value, technology-intensive segments to meet the burgeoning EV ecosystem needs.

forces.title: India Becoming Global Auto Component Sourcing Hub, Boosting Exports
forces.description: India is rapidly emerging as a global hub for auto component sourcing, with over 25% of its production exported annually. Exports are projected to reach US$ 70-100 billion by FY30, driven by increasing demand for electric vehicle (EV) technologies and global supply chain diversification efforts. This trend signifies a significant upside driver for the auto components sector, enhancing its international presence, fostering manufacturing capabilities, and securing long-term revenue growth from global markets.

forces.title: India's Competitive Advantages Boost Auto Component Manufacturing
forces.description: India benefits from strong competitive advantages that serve as a tailwind for the auto component industry. These include a substantial working-age population, providing a vast workforce (875 million forecast for manufacturing), strong political stability (7.1/10 in 2024), and strategic geographical proximity to key automotive markets such as ASEAN, Europe, Japan, and Korea. These factors collectively enhance India's appeal as a manufacturing and sourcing hub, fostering growth, investment, and export opportunities for auto component producers.

forces.title: Rising Trade Deficit Reflects Auto Component Import Dependence
forces.description: India's auto component industry experienced a trade deficit of US$ 180 million in H1 FY26, a reversal from a US$ 150 million surplus in H1 FY25. Exports grew by 9.3% to US$ 12.1 billion, while imports increased by a higher rate of 12.5% to US$ 12.3 billion. This growing deficit highlights a continued dependence on imports for certain critical components, posing a key risk to domestic value chain control and potentially impacting long-term profitability and supply chain resilience for manufacturers.

forces.title: Surging Investments and FDI Drive Auto Sector Growth
forces.description: India's automotive sector is attracting significant capital, with leading automakers planning approximately Rs 40,000 crore (US$ 4.23 billion) in capital expenditure for capacity expansion and EV adoption. The sector has cumulatively attracted Rs 2,70,230 crore (US$ 40.31 billion) in equity FDI between April 2000 and March 2026. India is projected to become the largest EV market by 2030, with an investment potential exceeding US$ 200 billion over the next five years, acting as a massive upside driver for growth.

forces.title: India-UK Trade Deal Reduces PV Tariffs, Boosts Local Industry
forces.description: The India-United Kingdom (UK) trade deal, signed in July 2025, represents a significant tailwind for the Indian passenger vehicle (PV) industry. It reduces import tariffs on fully built passenger vehicles from 100% to 10% over ten years, coupled with calibrated annual quotas. This agreement is expected to boost the Indian auto sector's domestic competitiveness by encouraging localisation, fostering innovation, and driving technology upgrades, while also providing access to new market opportunities.

forces.title: Robust Government Policy Support for EV & Auto Components Ecosystem
forces.description: The Indian government provides comprehensive policy support, including the PLI-Auto and PLI-ACC schemes, PM E-DRIVE (US$ 1.30 billion outlay) to accelerate EV adoption and charging infrastructure, FAME-II additional funding (US$ 180.3 million), PM-eBus Sewa Scheme (Rs 20,000 crore support), 100% customs duty exemption on critical EV minerals, and a DPIIT MoU with Ather Energy to boost the EV startup ecosystem. These initiatives create a strong tailwind, fostering a favorable environment for growth, innovation, and investment across the entire Automobiles & Components industry, especially for electric mobility.

viewpoints.title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry Poised for Strong 8-9% Growth in FY27
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings expects the Indian auto ancillary industry to grow by 8-9% in FY27, reaching a market size of Rs 10,681 billion. This positive outlook is driven by healthy vehicle production across PV, CV, and 2W segments, increasing component content per vehicle, resilient aftermarket demand, higher localisation efforts, and stronger integration with global supply chains. The transition towards electrification and advanced electronics is creating new, high-value opportunities for component manufacturers, with government policies like PLI-Auto and PM E-DRIVE schemes accelerating domestic capacity.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: Multi-Pathway Mobility Transition Offers Broad Opportunities Beyond Pure EVs
viewpoints.description: CareEdge highlights that India's mobility transition will likely remain multi-pathway, extending beyond pure electric vehicles to include hybrids, flex-fuel vehicles, ethanol-blended platforms, CNG vehicles, and potential hydrogen-based technologies. This diversified approach creates significant opportunities for automotive component manufacturers across a wider range of product categories, including advanced fuel systems, emission-control technologies, sensors, electronic control units, and lightweight materials, ensuring sustained growth even as EV adoption accelerates.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: AI to Redefine Automotive Retail Battle by Enhancing Customer Experience
viewpoints.description: KPMG's Jeffry Jacob asserts that artificial intelligence will become as critical to automotive retail as electrification, shifting competitive differentiation from product features to superior customer experiences. As EV adoption introduces new decision frameworks, AI can transform vehicle retailing into a personalized advisory experience, helping dealers understand diverse customer needs, recommend tailored solutions, and build confidence, which is essential for mass-market EV adoption in India's competitive dealership ecosystem.
viewpoints.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

viewpoints.title: Auto Ancillary Industry Entering Sustained Investment-Led Growth Phase in India
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings expresses a positive outlook for the Indian auto ancillary industry, noting it is entering a sustained investment-led growth phase. This growth is supported by expanding domestic vehicle production, increasing value addition across the automotive supply chain, and the transition towards electronics-intensive and cleaner mobility platforms, which are expanding addressable markets. Localisation initiatives are creating opportunities to reduce import dependence, and established cost pass-through mechanisms with OEMs provide earnings resilience.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: India's Auto Component Industry Positioned for Larger Global Sourcing Share
viewpoints.description: Ranjan Sharma, Senior Director at CareEdge Ratings, emphasizes India's auto component industry has become an increasingly vital part of the global automotive supply chain, backed by manufacturing competitiveness, strong engineering capabilities, and a rapidly expanding domestic market. With the industry projected to exceed Rs 10.6 trillion in market size by FY27, the sector is well-positioned to capture a larger share of global sourcing opportunities, with continued localisation and advanced manufacturing being key for value enhancement.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: Global Automotive Industry Facing Transformation from Intelligence Age, Volatility
viewpoints.description: Dr. Andreas Ries, Global Head of Automotive at KPMG International, states the global automotive industry is at a critical juncture where the 'Intelligence Age,' driven by AI and advanced software, is fundamentally reshaping products, value chains, and competitive advantages. Simultaneously, geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain volatility are intensifying strategic and operational pressures. This necessitates adaptive strategies, disciplined execution, and a commitment to integrating technology with workforce development to navigate disruption and unlock new opportunities.

viewpoints.title: Automotive Leaders Prioritise Data Resilience and Local Capability for Growth
viewpoints.description: Dr. Andreas Ries, Global Head of Automotive at KPMG International, notes that automotive companies are adopting a disciplined approach by prioritizing the strengthening of data resilience, national sovereignty, and local capabilities before pursuing targeted growth initiatives. This strategic sequencing is intended to de-risk operations and enable future expansion under tighter governance and financial control, indicating a mature response to ongoing global volatility and supply chain uncertainties.

viewpoints.title: Geopolitical Volatility Accelerating Tech Transformation and De-risking in Auto
viewpoints.description: KPMG's analysis challenges the notion that geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility will derail technological progress in the automotive industry. Instead, the data indicates that uncertainty is acting as a catalyst, accelerating transformation. Companies are intensifying investments in digital and software foundations, strengthening data capabilities, and increasing strategic independence. This approach leverages technology not as a retreat, but as a proactive mechanism for de-risking operations and supply chains amidst persistent external shocks.

viewpoints.title: Indian EV Market Set for Robust, Steady Growth Driven by Government Support
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports that India's electric vehicle (EV) market is poised for 'strong and steady' growth through 2030. This optimistic outlook is attributed to a significant shift in focus by companies towards the EV segment, coupled with robust and proactive government leadership. These factors are creating a conducive environment for widespread EV adoption and expanding the overall market size and penetration across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and passenger vehicle segments in the country.

viewpoints.title: India Emerges as Global Leader in Electric Two and Three-Wheeler Manufacturing
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights India's prominent position as the largest manufacturer of electric two-wheelers (E2W) and electric three-wheelers (E3W) globally. This leadership underscores India's significant progress and manufacturing capabilities within the electric mobility segment, particularly in high-utilization vehicle categories. This capability is supported by strong domestic demand, policy incentives, and a growing ecosystem for EV components and infrastructure, solidifying India's role in the global EV landscape.

viewpoints.title: India's Auto Component Sector Targets $145 Billion Production by 2030
viewpoints.description: IBEF outlines an ambitious yet attainable vision for India's automotive sector by 2030, projecting auto component production to reach US$ 145 billion. This growth is expected to triple exports from US$ 20 billion to US$ 60 billion, thereby elevating India’s share in the global automotive value chain from 3% to 8%. This reflects robust demand drivers, competitive advantages like a skilled workforce, and comprehensive policy support aimed at boosting manufacturing and advanced component production.

demand_drivers.description: Anticipated healthy volume growth across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, and two-wheelers during FY27.
Growing preference for SUVs and premium vehicles, coupled with stricter safety and emissions norms, increases demand for higher-value systems.
Supported by an expanding vehicle parc, rising average vehicle age, premiumisation, and increasing demand for replacement parts and regular maintenance.
Continued integration with global automotive supply chains and efforts to reduce import dependence on critical automotive technologies.

market_sizing.methodology: India’s auto-component industry is poised to reach US$ 200 billion by 2030.
Automobile component industry turnover in H1 FY26 stood at Rs 3,56,193 crore (US$ 41.20 billion). Domestic OEM supplies contributed ~66%, domestic aftermarket ~11%, and exports ~23%.
Auto component supplies to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) reached Rs 3,04,663 crore (US$ 35.20 billion) in H1 FY26.
The aftermarket segment for auto components was valued at Rs 53,160 crore (US$ 6.10 billion) in H1 FY26.

The Indian EV battery market is expected to expand from US$ 2.71 billion in 2025 to US$ 15.90 billion by 2034.
